title: Franc-jeu Hosts Foreign Minister on Sunday
seoTitle: Franc-jeu: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot Interview
subtitle: Benjamin Duhamel to interview Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs on public TV
excerpt: This Sunday, October 4, 2026, France 2's Franc-jeu program will host Jean-Noël Barrot, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The political program Franc-jeu, usually broadcast on Sundays at noon on France 2, takes center stage this week by hosting Jean-Noël Barrot, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, for a live interview. This particular episode, scheduled for 1:20 PM, comes at a time of intense discussions about French foreign policy and the approaching 2027 presidential election.

Who is Sunday's Guest?

Jean-Noël Barrot holds the portfolio for Europe and Foreign Affairs, coordinating France's international policy. His role includes managing external crises, relations with European institutions, and defining diplomatic strategies that directly affect the country's position on the continent.

Anticipated Interview Topics

During Franc-jeu, Barrot is expected to answer questions from Benjamin Duhamel regarding the current international crisis, the war on the continent's borders, and the impacts of these situations on the upcoming presidential elections. The emphasis will be on French diplomacy, European priorities, and the decisions shaping the foreign agenda in the coming months.

Broadcast Time and Platforms

The broadcast begins at 1:20 PM on France 2 and will be simultaneously aired on France Inter, the france.tv website, and the international channel TV5MONDE. The same content will be available via streaming, allowing the public to follow the interview on computers, tablets, or smartphones. For those who miss the live broadcast, the program will be available for replay on the france.tv platform.

Relevance for the 2027 Presidential Campaign

With the presidential election scheduled for 2027, Barrot's interview gains greater importance, as his responses could influence voters' perceptions of the conduct of foreign policy. The live debate offers a platform for the minister to clarify stances and strategies that citizens will be able to evaluate at the polls.

Public and Debate Expectations

The direct and clear format adopted by Benjamin Duhamel aims to bring public debate closer to government decisions. Simultaneous broadcasting on TV, radio, and the internet expands national coverage, allowing the program to reach diverse audiences, from those watching at home to those following the interview while on the move.

With information from Linternaute.com, Télé Star.
